clue.text: Versatile computer program making me angry! (13, two words)

parts.note: cross is an everyday word for annoyed
the one making this puzzle, the setter speaking as 'me', is its compiler

explanation.surface: A user rages at a supposedly versatile piece of software that keeps infuriating them.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as a complaint, but 'me' is the setter, and a crossword setter is also called a compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-compiler is a program that builds code on one platform to run on another, hence versatile across machines.

clue.text: Fraudulent daily has drunk alicant

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a woman who cleans someone's house each day

indicators.note: someone drunk is unsteady and muddled, so the letters of the following word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dishonest newspaper reports that it has been knocking back Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' suggests a newspaper; it is the British term for a cleaning lady. Alicant is an old name for a wine from Alicante.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlatanic describes the conduct of a charlatan, a quack or impostor, and so means deceitful or fraudulent.

clue.text: Top Rugby contest (6, two words)

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
a bout is a contest, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A leading rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective meaning best, but it is the slang verb meaning to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang, to top someone and to rub someone out both mean to murder them.

clue.text: Wrestler, American, turning up with muscle I'll follow

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US citizen
a motor is a muscle that moves a part of the body
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American wrestler arrives with his own muscle, and the speaker trails along behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sumotori is a sumo wrestler, the Japanese name for a competitor in sumo.

clue.text: Dryasdust when disturbed may become so obstinate — sad

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so its letters are rearranged
the dash reads as minus, so the word after it is subtracted from the shuffled letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written: these letters are subtracted

explanation.surface: A dull pedant, once upset, may turn stubborn and gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus the word sad together rearrange to Dryasdust, the name of a dreary pedant from Scott's prefaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides robust, sturdy has the older sense of stubborn or resolute, as in sturdy refusal, so it can mean obstinate.

clue.text: Finishing touches: cut lettuce with knife

indicators.note: cut means sliced open, so the next item is pushed into the gap

parts.note: cos is a long-leaved lettuce
a da, or dah, is a heavy Burmese knife

explanation.surface: The last step in making a salad: slicing the lettuce with a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is a closing passage in music or literature, so codas round off and complete a work.

clue.text: Law experts must, if mistaken

indicators.note: a mistaken version is a garbled one, so the letters before it are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lawyers are required to admit it whenever they get something wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' is both part of the anagram signal and part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mufti is a Muslim scholar qualified to issue rulings on Islamic law.

clue.text: Name of bird genus, one given below illustration

parts.note: pic is short for picture
a means one, as in a dozen

explanation.surface: A naturalist's note on a bird's genus, with a caption placed under its picture.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece given below another follows it in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pica is the Latin generic name of the magpies, so it names a genus of birds.

clue.text: Start of lambing, distress for highland fold

indicators.note: Start of keeps just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter
to irk is to trouble or annoy

explanation.surface: The beginning of lambing season brings worry to a sheepfold in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' suggests a sheep pen; it means a crease, and lirk is the Scots word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a lirk is a crease or wrinkle in cloth or skin, so it is a fold in the highland tongue.

clue.text: Play bill in English theatre (now renamed)

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: in puts the item before it inside the letters that follow

parts.note: NT was the National Theatre, since renamed the Royal National Theatre
ac is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A playbill on display at an English theatre that has changed its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play bill' reads as one item, the theatre programme, but splits into the definition and a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a part is to act or perform it on stage, so enact means play.

clue.text: Agent peers nervously inside letter?

indicators.note: inside places the shuffled letters within the word that follows

parts.note: a letter here is one who lets property, a renter

indicators.note: acting nervously means fidgeting, so the letters before it move about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A secret agent peeps anxiously into an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like a written message; it is someone who lets out property.
explanation.definitionFit: A representer is one who acts on behalf of another, which is what an agent does.

clue.text: Rondavel universal for Bantu speaker?

parts.note: a rondavel is a round thatched hut of southern Africa
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Asks whether a round African hut suits everyone who speaks a Bantu language.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu of Rwanda and Burundi speak Kinyarwanda and Kirundi, which belong to the Bantu family; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Dilution changed last of vegetable dye component

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the word before it are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: last of asks for only the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of vegetable

explanation.surface: A dye recipe in which watering down changed the vegetable ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Toluidine is an aromatic amine used as an intermediate in making many synthetic dyes.

clue.text: Confuse big bird held in bond

indicators.note: something held in is enclosed, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: bd is the dictionary abbreviation for bond
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A large bird stuck in some kind of bond, a baffling picture.
explanation.walkthrough: BEMUD is a rare word in Chambers: literally to bespatter with mud, figuratively to confuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemud is to muddy, and figuratively to muddle or befog someone's thinking.

clue.text: Dog: not one goes round free when brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from bottom to top
going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: non is the Latin-derived prefix meaning not
a means one
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A dog roams loose, circling, when it is brought up from somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' points to a pet, but a firedog is a metal stand that holds logs in a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is one of a pair of iron supports for logs on a hearth, also called a firedog or dog.

clue.text: Tropical tree in decline? Not me, making comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the remaining letters are read in the opposite direction
Not tells us the word right after it is to be left out of what comes before

parts.note: paracme is the stage at which a fever or disease declines
taken as written: these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A tropical tree in decline, with the speaker disowning any part in its revival.
explanation.walkthrough: PARACME is a rare medical word for the declining phase of a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Carap is the crab-wood, a tropical American tree of the genus Carapa, valued for timber and seed oil.

clue.text: Pick-me-up to take from prayer?

parts.note: to rob is to take something from someone
an orant is a figure shown praying, arms raised, in early Christian art

explanation.surface: Asks whether a reviving tonic is something you might steal from a person at prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A roborant is a strengthening tonic or restorative medicine, which is just what a pick-me-up is.

clue.text: Dull stuff about char's 'enzyme'

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: prose can mean dull, commonplace talk or writing
char is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A dreary article about a cleaning lady's so-called enzyme.
explanation.definitionFit: A protease is an enzyme that breaks down proteins, so the answer names a kind of enzyme.

clue.text: Double helpings of lunch stew will satisfy this appetite

indicators.note: a helping taken twice means two letters are served from the front of each word

parts.note: the opening pair of letters
the opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: Two big portions of stew at lunch will fill up the hungriest diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lust can mean a strong craving or relish of any kind, as in a lust for life, so appetite fits.

clue.text: It's dear reshaping bust

indicators.note: reshaping means changing the form, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Remodelling a sculpted bust turns out to be expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a sculpture or a bosom, but here it is the verb meaning to demote.
explanation.definitionFit: To bust someone, in military slang, is to reduce them in rank, and to disrate is to lower a sailor's rating.

clue.text: Nothing in past encore heralds leap for 'elevated' chorister? (9, two words)

indicators.note: a herald comes first and announces what follows, so one piece goes directly before the next
in places the first item inside the word that follows it

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by
the zero-shaped letter
bis, Latin for twice, is called out for an encore
a hop is a small leap

explanation.surface: A cryptic chain of nothing, the past, an encore and a leap.
explanation.walkthrough: A boy bishop was a choirboy elected as mock bishop for St Nicholas's Day to Holy Innocents in medieval churches, so he is raised in rank only in jest.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation marks show the chorister's promotion to bishop is a temporary festive custom rather than a real consecration.

clue.text: Feel very sorry for old governor going round mine

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: a bey was a governor of a province in the Ottoman Empire
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Pity the former colonial governor, forced to make the rounds of a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bepity is an old intensive form of pity, meaning to pity greatly or show deep compassion.

clue.text: Difficult to take in fuel, we hear? This is used to launch rocket

definitions.text: This is used to launch rocket

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words before it are to be judged by their sound

parts.note: a hard task is one set high, and to dine is to take in fuel

explanation.surface: Something hard to refuel, perhaps, used to send a rocket aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound-alike is loose: it rests on reading difficult as high and taking in fuel as dining.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydyne was a liquid rocket propellant used in the Jupiter-C that launched America's first satellite, Explorer 1.

clue.text: One is used for cradling hybrids endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: crosses are hybrids produced by interbreeding

explanation.surface: A cradle that keeps rocking cross-bred infants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cradling' suggests a baby, but in lacrosse it is the cradling of the ball in the stick's net.
explanation.definitionFit: The crosse is the netted stick of lacrosse, rocked from side to side to cradle the ball while running.

clue.text: Tip? Not one penny given to most backward waiter

indicators.note: Not removes the items named right after it from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
p is the abbreviation for a penny
read as a superlative of arrear, an old word for backward or behind

explanation.surface: A customer refuses even a penny's tip to the slowest waiter in the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiter' suggests someone serving tables, but here it means anyone who waits. The second half of the wordplay is the least certain part of this parse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarrier is one who tarries, that is, someone who lingers or delays, and so literally a waiter.

clue.text: Tropical fruits not consumed by those trying to abstain

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed, so it ends up inside what follows

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members try to stay off drink
non is the prefix meaning not

explanation.surface: Tropical fruits that people on a diet steer clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: Anona, or annona, is the genus of custard apples and soursops, so it stands for those tropical fruits.

clue.text: One with raised cane, offering varying choices (5, two words)

parts.note: an means one, as in an apple

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: a rod is a stick or cane

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster with raised cane offers the culprit a choice of punishments.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase and/or offers either option or both together, so it presents a choice of alternatives.

clue.text: One may have classed — as source of scarlet dyes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a vehicle wheel's rubber cover, which is graded by load and speed class
second meaning: the Phoenician port famous for its murex dyes

explanation.surface: Something graded into a class turns out to be where rich red dyes came from.
explanation.walkthrough: The ancient city in Lebanon gave its name to Tyrian purple, a crimson-to-purple dye from murex shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lebanese seaport was the ancient centre of dyeing with murex, producing the costly crimson Tyrian purple.

clue.text: Health food laced with alcohol died away

indicators.note: away means gone, so the word just before it is taken out

parts.note: a dish laced with alcohol might be brandied
taken as written: these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone's healthy diet was spiked with drink and the eater passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'died away' reads as one phrase meaning faded; it splits into the letters to remove and the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran, the husk of cereal grain, is eaten as a high-fibre aid to digestion and so counts as a health food.

clue.text: Gathering belt up I run

parts.note: belt up is British slang for be quiet
taken as written
r is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A runner at a rally tightens their belt before the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Shir, a variant of shirr, is a gathering of fabric drawn up on parallel threads in sewing.

clue.text: Contemplate lake (small) with wader 'aunting it? (8, two words)

indicators.note: the dropped aitch in the spelling of haunting shows the bird's name loses its own opening aitch

parts.note: a pond is a small lake
the heron is a long-legged wading bird

explanation.surface: Picture a little lake with a heron haunting its edge, inviting quiet thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a Cockney voice that drops its aitches, 'pond heron' becomes the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder on something is to think about it deeply, which is to contemplate it.

clue.text: Up in Watten or Thurso

indicators.note: in says the answer is sitting inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first town, the word or, and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A question about what 'up' means in two small towns in the far north of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Watten and Thurso are in Caithness, at the very top of mainland Scotland, which makes the hidden word apt.
explanation.definitionFit: On a conventional map the top is the northern edge, so up stands for the compass direction.

clue.text: E. Asian tribals had reduced beasts of burden

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so only a contracted form of the word before it is kept

parts.note: taken as written, then contracted to its apostrophe form
yaks are Himalayan oxen used to carry loads

explanation.surface: Some Asian tribespeople used to keep pack animals, though fewer now.
explanation.walkthrough: Had shortens to 'd, as in I'd.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dyaks, or Dayaks, are indigenous peoples of Borneo in the Malay Archipelago of south-east Asia.

clue.text: A bug found in privy to become one result of intestinal disease

indicators.note: found in says the first items are discovered inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: being in on a secret is being privy to it
taken as written
a nit is a louse egg, a small bug
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A germ lurking in the lavatory turns into a symptom of a gut infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'privy' looks like a toilet, but with 'to' it means being in on a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanition is exhaustion from lack of nourishment, which follows when a diseased gut cannot absorb food.

clue.text: Variant Shakespeare reading? I am rejected by some orientals

indicators.note: rejected by means thrown out of, so these words are taken out of the next word

parts.note: the Siamese are the people of Siam, now Thailand
taken as written: these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean textual puzzle in which the speaker is snubbed by people from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgar's cry 'sessa' in King Lear is printed in this shorter form in some early texts.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors print this form as an alternative text for Edgar's exclamation in King Lear, so it is a variant reading.

clue.text: Grass snake? It's found climbing in the Andes perhaps

definitions.text: It's found climbing in the Andes perhaps

parts.note: both grass and canary are slang for an informer, one who sings to the police
a snake creeps along the ground, so is a creeper

explanation.surface: A question about whether a grass snake might be seen climbing in the Andes.
explanation.walkthrough: A grass snake is a common European snake, but 'grass' here is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Canary creeper, Tropaeolum peregrinum, is a yellow-flowered climbing nasturtium native to the Andes of Peru and Ecuador.
